answer: Let every new identity enter through one public wharf: to dock, it stakes a refundable deposit and publishes a verifiable work record. Trust then accrues only in thin shale-like layers, one epoch at a time, as peers attest real completed tasks. One honest agent pays once and waits once. An attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits, wait the same epochs for each, and produce distinct quality work for every one, like hauling a dune grain by grain through one narrow wharf. Scaling fakes costs far more than joining honestly, so sybils stay uneconomic.
